newsitem.title: FRANCE: French growth to be stronger than expected-Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: French growth to be stronger than expected-Arthuis.

text.p: The French economy will grow more strongly than expected, benefiting from low interest rates and a benign dollar/franc exchange rate, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said Sunday.

"We have a fortunate set of circumstances for our economy and I think growth will be stronger than we imagined, than we expected," he said on television station TF1. "And in these conditions, we will be able to create more jobs."
"Interest rates have never been so low; rates are the lowest for 35 years," he said. "Parities -- I'm thinking of the dollar for example -- have never been so good for France."
He gave no detailed growth forecast.
On January 16 Arthuis said he expected the economy to grow at least 2.3 percent this year.
A Finance Ministry official said last Thursday that the overall financial and monetary outlook in Europe was positive and domestic growth should be fairly robust from the start of 1997.

National Statistics Office said last week consumer spending on manufactured goods fell 0.8 percent in December after dropping 0.5 percent in November, giving an overall drop of 3.4 percent in the last quarter of 1996.

France needs solid growth to cut its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product from four percent last year to join the single European currency and combat unemployment, running at a record 12.7 percent.
